author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing treats a page value below 1 as the first page
summary: Opening the owner listing with a page value below 1 renders the error page today. The listing must treat any such value as the first page and respond with the normal listing.
acceptance_criteria: Given a page value of 0, -1, the most negative value an integer holds (-2147483648), or a negative number too large for an integer (-99999999999), when /owners opens, then the response is HTTP 200 with the normal owner listing, not the error page.
Given a page value below 1 and more than one matching owner, when the listing renders, then it shows the first page of owners and reports the first page as the current page.

Given a last-name search with a page value below 1, when it runs, then the outcome matches the same search on the first page: several matches list their first page, one match opens that owner's record, and no match reports that no owner was found.
Given a page value of 1 or above, or no page value, when the listing opens, then behavior is unchanged.
non_goals: The veterinarian directory's paging: the request names the owner listing only. Recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md.
Non-numeric page values and page values past the last page: the request names values below 1 only. Recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md.
notes: Scope grounds in the intake request at handoff line 1; its decisions list is empty. No Non-Goals row or existing requirement conflicts, so no consultation was needed. The request's 'any page value below 1' is read literally, so a negative number too large for an integer is in scope. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records. docs/ubiquitous-language.md is unchanged: no new domain term.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The fix stays in OwnerController: architecture-principles § pattern catalog, Web controller row, classes normalizing a request parameter to its permitted range as binding, not a business rule. docs/system-design.md Contracts now assign it there and add REQ-OWN-005 to the OwnerController row. Adjustment: the page request parameter widens from int to BigInteger, because int cannot bind a negative value below the integer minimum (observed 400 for -99999999999). Normalize once at the top of processFindForm into a local int; findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel keep their int signatures and both receive the normalized value, so currentPage reports the first page. Cause observed on the running app (bootRun, curl; grep-level basis, IDE oracle not connected): 0, -1 and -2147483648 return 500 from PageRequest.of(page - 1, ...) or its int overflow; -99999999999 returns 400 from type mismatch.
integration_points: Binding: GET /owners gains no new entry point; the page parameter binds to a request-scoped BigInteger scalar with its default of 1 kept. The Owner search binding is unchanged.
Double, framework transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned harness (testing-principles § Mocking Policy).

Double, OwnerRepository: the class's existing @MockitoBean, a framework stub by recorded exception. @WebMvcTest needs the bean and a hand-written double would implement all of JpaRepository. Stub with a matcher accepting only page number 0, never any(Pageable.class), so a wrong page yields an empty result and the outcome assertion fails (testing-principles § A stub is a stand-in). Do not copy the page size into the test.

patterns.description: Parameter normalization is binding and stays in the controller; do not extract a service or helper type for it.
A rule assigned to the web controller is tested at the web level through MockMvc.
processFindForm, the single seam for the change.

risks.risk: Normalizing after the page - 1 subtraction, or with arithmetic on the raw value, lets -2147483648 overflow to a huge positive page (Contracts, OwnerController row).
risks.mitigation: Compare against 1 before any subtraction; only the normalized int reaches the helpers.

risks.risk: Widening the parameter changes outcomes outside the slice. Observed today: abc, 2147483648 and 99999999999 return 400; prd-entry acceptance criterion 4 and non_goals keep them unchanged. A bare BigInteger.intValueExact would turn oversized positives into 500 (architecture-principles § Web controller row).
risks.mitigation: Non-numeric values keep failing in framework binding. A value above the integer maximum raises ResponseStatusException with BAD_REQUEST and no reason text, keeping the 400 and the error page. Add regression tests beyond the prd-entry names for abc and 2147483648.

risks.risk: Widening to long would satisfy the -99999999999 example yet fail a longer negative number, which the request's any page value below 1 includes (Contracts, OwnerController row).
risks.mitigation: Bind BigInteger; include a negative value beyond the long range in the parameterized case.

risks.risk: BigInteger parsing cost grows with digit count on an untrusted query value (security-principles § Trust Boundaries).
risks.mitigation: The servlet container's request-header limit bounds the query length; no additional control needed. No request value enters an exception message (security-principles § Language Realization, secret disclosure row).

risks.risk: Owner listing and last-name search scales with owners (§ Scale and Load, Owner listing row).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: the database-paged query is unchanged.

notes: Writes: docs/system-design.md OwnerController row, plus a new § Scale and Load section with one row. The section was absent from the brief; the design-validation checklist and the doctor template both expect it, and the row uses unrecorded, treated as bounded. No ADR: the choice is contained in this slice. Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records. page=2147483647 returns 500 today (observed); it is an existing past-the-last-page outcome, left unchanged and within the PRD open question. Veterinarian paging stays out of scope per non_goals. ubiquitous-language unchanged.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Conjectural path, not demonstrated in this review: the design-block's bound on BigInteger parsing cost rests on the container's request-header limit, which holds for the query string (grep of application*.properties for max-http, server. and tomcat found no override, so the default applies). A query-string value of that size is harmless. The unverified question is whether a `page` value can arrive by another carrier: a GET to /owners with a multipart/form-data body, if multipart resolution runs for GET and Tomcat exposes the form part as a request parameter, would be bounded by the far larger form-post limit rather than the header limit, and `new BigInteger(String)` cost grows faster than linearly with digit count (JDK parsing behavior from recall). This change introduces that cost, because the previous int binding failed fast on long input. The multipart auto-configuration defaults, Tomcat 11.0.27 parameter handling, and JDK 25 parse timing were not verified here: the permitted commands exclude running the application. Worth one probe against the running app with a roughly 2 MB digit string in a multipart `page` field. If it stalls a request thread for seconds, the slice owes a length bound before parsing; the placement of that bound is a design question.
approved_aspects: Boundary range check (security-principles Trust Boundaries, external input row): OwnerController.java:132 `if (page.compareTo(BigInteger.ONE) < 0) {` runs before any arithmetic and OwnerController.java:135 `if (page.compareTo(LARGEST_PAGE) > 0) {` rejects above the integer maximum, so `page.intValue()` at line 138 cannot truncate and `PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize)` at line 152 receives a value of at least 0 with no overflow. The -2147483648 overflow path is closed.

Error disclosure: OwnerController.java:136 `throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST);` carries no reason text and no request value. error.html:18 `

Exception message

` renders with escaping, so the error page, which shows the exception message, gains no new sensitive or reflected content from this change.

Template sink: `currentPage` receives only the normalized int (OwnerController.java:128 and :143). The four `__${...}__` preprocessing expressions in owners/ownersList.html (grep -E '__\$\{' counted 4) were not changed by this diff and evaluate integers, never request text.

Query path: no data-access code changed. The normalized value reaches the existing Pageable at a fixed page size of 5 (OwnerController.java:151 `int pageSize = 5;`), so a value below 1 costs exactly one first-page query, the same as an ordinary page=1 request, with no amplification. A bound parameter reaches no filesystem, shell, or query text.

Binding surface: `page` remains a request-scoped scalar. The @InitBinder at OwnerController.java:66 `dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id");` is unchanged and no check, annotation, or escaping call was removed. No endpoint was added, so the exposed surface is not widened.

Credentials and dependencies: a case-insensitive grep of the added diff lines for token, password, passwd, secret, api key, credential, jdbc: and bearer returned no hits. The changed-file list contains no build file (grep for build.gradle, pom.xml, gradle.properties and libs.versions counted 0), so no dependency changed.

Supply chain: no dependency vulnerability scan ran, the standing gap in security-principles.md Standing Gaps. Versions read from `./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath`: Spring Boot 4.1.2, jackson-databind 3.1.7, tomcat-embed-core 11.0.27.

IDE oracle not connected in this headless run. No access-control or route-exposure claim here turns on symbol resolution; the BigInteger sweep used grep (OwnerController.java is the only request binding of BigInteger under src/main/java), the weaker basis.

author: change-grader
summary: normalize owner listing page values below 1 to the first page

blast_radius.note: Production reach is one handler and one private helper in OwnerController, with 23 changed lines. VetController and the template are untouched, and the 21 hunks are mostly imports, test code and two doc files. The row lists no sensitive path, though it does flag the controller as declared security surface, which the semantic surprise facet covers.

semantic_surprise.note: The clamp itself reads correctly: it compares before any subtraction, only the normalized int reaches the helpers, and values from 1 to the integer maximum pass through unchanged. The surprise is the type widening. int binding failed fast on long input, while new BigInteger does a quadratic parse of attacker-sized digits, and that parse runs during binding, before normalizePage can reject anything. The design bounds this by the request-header limit, which does not cover a multipart carrier: read statically, Spring's isMultipart has no HTTP method check and Tomcat's parseParts adds form fields to request parameters under its post-size limit, not the header limit. Reachability and stall time are unmeasured.

test_adequacy.note: Tests are real: pageNumbered stubs answer only the correct page, so a wrong page fails on outcome, and rows cover 0, -1, the integer minimum, and values below the integer and long ranges, plus a pass-through and a 400 row just above the maximum. Two gaps are acceptable after reading the code. The one-match and no-match outcomes at page below 1 lost their tests in the fix round, but those branches never read page. The Integer.MAX_VALUE row asserts 200 against a stub, while the design observed a 500 on the running app, so it pins pass-through only, not the real outcome.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers approved and every citation I checked resolves, including OwnerController.java lines 132 to 138, 151 and 152, error.html:18, architecture-principles.md:85 and prd.md:181-182. But the security-reviewer's approval carries an explicitly unverified recommendation: a large multipart page value may stall a request thread, and if so the slice owes a length bound before parsing. Nobody ran the probe, and the fix round re-dispatched only the test-reviewer, so it stayed open. The test-reviewer's two recommendations are minor: the 400 test characterizes an open PRD question, and the declared-test list is stale.

scope_deviation.note: The change stays within triage: zero retries, consultations and design revisions, with the vet directory, non-numeric and past-last-page behavior left as recorded open questions. The above-maximum 400 branch preserves today's outcome and is placed by the design-block. The new Scale and Load section goes past the bug report but is recorded in the design-block. The fix round only deleted two tests, with no production change, though prd-entry test_names still lists them.

rationale: The page clamp is correct and contained. The residual is the BigInteger binding: an untrusted page value now gets a quadratic parse before any check, and the security reviewer's multipart caveat was never probed. Run that probe, then decide whether a length bound is owed before merging.
